finding.claim: The admin check in ban() is wrapped in try/except Exception, so abort(403) from require_admin is swallowed and do_ban(uid) runs for non-admin users. Any user whose g.user dict lacks is_admin can ban arbitrary users and receives {"ok": true}.
finding.source: POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban from any session where g.user is a dict without is_admin (ordinary authenticated user); uid taken from URL path
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 (protected user-ban operation; body is a stub at admin.py:31-32)

trace.note: Only logs a warning; execution continues

finding.guards_checked: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) raises 403 but is neutralized by except Exception at admin.py:18; no decorator, before_request, or blueprint guard in the file; unban (admin.py:24-28) has no try and correctly enforces admin, showing the try in ban is the defect; if g.user is unset, AttributeError at line 19 yields 500 and do_ban is not reached, so the bypass requires g.user to be a dict. Not verifiable from this file: middleware that populates g.user, CSRF protection for POST routes, and the real do_ban implementation.

verdict.guard_found: none. require_admin (admin.py:9-11) raises via abort(403), but its result is never tested and its exception is caught by the bare `except Exception:` at admin.py:18, so execution falls through to do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20. No decorator, before_request, or blueprint guard exists in this file. The unban route at admin.py:26 calls require_admin without a try and does enforce the check.
verdict.reason: The defect is real: require_admin raises 403 at admin.py:10-11, the `except Exception:` at admin.py:18 swallows it, and do_ban(uid) runs at admin.py:20 for any caller whose g.user is a dict without is_admin, so an ordinary authenticated user can ban arbitrary users. The trace is off by one in one entry: the require_admin(g.user) call is at admin.py:17, not 16 (line 16 is `try:`), which is why trace_ok is false, but the logic described is accurate at the correct lines.
